name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Open floor — any agent from any department: name the single best cross-department improvement to make right now, and who should do it.

name: Reel
text: Standardize real-time transcription for all pending videos using Deepgram. It’s the fastest way to get accurate transcripts into the pipeline without manual delays. The trade-off is higher short-term API costs, but the speed and quality gains outweigh the expense.

name: Scriv
text: Deepgram’s real-time transcription isn’t the bottleneck—it’s the 14-day fixed A/B test that’s wasting time and risking bad decisions. The real cross-department fix is to shorten the A/B test window to 48 hours with a rolling sample, owned by the data science team. That’s the only change that cuts both delay and risk.

name: Chisel
text:
Run a 48-hour rolling A/B test on the 200k clips with Whisper batch processing instead of the 14-day fixed window. This cuts decision latency from weeks to days, letting us iterate faster without sacrificing statistical rigor. The trade-off is accepting slightly noisier early data, but the speed gain for the whole pipeline outweighs the risk. Data science owns this change.
[dispatched 2 workers: worker-9213, worker-9672 — done, dissolved]

name: Sift
text: The 48-hour rolling A/B test on 200k clips with Whisper batch processing risks false positives from Whisper’s batch latency and fixed A/B window mismatch. Instead, run a 72-hour *overlapping* A/B test with real-time Deepgram transcripts to validate both speed and accuracy. Settle it by comparing transcript quality and decision latency across both methods in a side-by-side pilot—if Deepgram’s transcripts hold up, drop Whisper entirely.

name: Scope
text: Run a 72-hour overlapping A/B test on 200k clips using real-time Deepgram transcripts. This cuts decision latency from weeks to three days while keeping statistical rigor intact—no false positives from batch delays. The trade-off is higher Deepgram API costs, but the speed and accuracy gains outweigh the expense. Data science owns the test design and validation.

name: Scriv
text: The 72-hour overlapping A/B test with Deepgram still risks false positives from overlapping sample contamination—two groups seeing the same clip at different times. The real fix is a strict 48-hour *non-overlapping* A/B test with Whisper batch processing, owned by data science, to eliminate sample bleed and cut latency without trading accuracy for speed. Settle it by running both tests in parallel for one day and comparing error rates—if Whisper’s batch delay doesn’t skew results, it’s the faster, cheaper path.

name: Reel
text: Run a strict 48-hour non-overlapping A/B test on 200k clips using Whisper batch processing, owned by data science. This cuts decision latency from weeks to two days with clean sample separation, eliminating false positives from overlapping or real-time delays. The trade-off is accepting slightly noisier early data from Whisper’s batch latency, but the speed and statistical rigor outweigh the cost.

name: Scriv
text: Whisper batch processing still introduces a 30-minute lag per batch—enough to skew results if user behavior shifts during that window. The real risk isn’t false positives from overlap; it’s delayed feedback masking true user impact. Settle it with a 48-hour *stratified* A/B test: split clips by traffic source, run Whisper in parallel with Deepgram real-time, and compare transcript accuracy *and* downstream metrics. Data science owns the design; engineering just executes.

name: Chisel
text: Run a 48-hour *stratified* A/B test on 200k clips with Whisper batch processing, owned by data science. Splitting clips by traffic volume and transcript length ensures clean separation and faster feedback than overlapping tests, while the stratification keeps the data representative. The trade-off is accepting a 30-minute batch lag, but the speed gain from a fixed 48-hour window outweighs the minor delay.

name: Sift
text: Stratification by traffic and transcript length won’t fix Whisper’s 30-minute batch lag—user behavior can shift faster than the batch can process, masking real impact. Settle it with a 24-hour *real-time* A/B test using Deepgram, accepting the cost to cut latency to one day and isolate true user effects.

name: Scope
text: Run a 24-hour real-time Deepgram A/B test on 200k clips, owned by data science. This cuts decision latency to one day while isolating true user impact—no batch lag, no overlap contamination, and no false positives from delayed feedback. The trade-off is higher Deepgram API costs, but speed and accuracy outweigh the expense.

name: Scriv
text: Deepgram’s real-time A/B test risks inflating costs without fixing Whisper’s core flaw: batch lag still masks user behavior shifts within the 24-hour window. Settle it with a 48-hour *stratified* Whisper batch test—split by traffic and transcript length—owned by data science. The trade-off is 30 minutes of lag, but it’s predictable and cheaper than Deepgram’s burn rate.
